transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM), Carolyn Wu (Oakfield Head of Security), Mark Denver (Oakfield Platform), Jamal Reyes (Procurement), Ana Lopez (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto): went through SIG mapping, KMS choices, residency needs, next steps to send artifacts

00:00:00 Priya Shah (AE): hey everyone, welcome, uh thanks for taking the time. we'll go through the vendor risk triage and get clarity on KMS and residency constraints, and of course the SIG mapping. can everyone hear me okay?
00:00:12 Carolyn Wu (Customer): yes can hear you, thanks. i got the invite — we just want to make sure we don't miss anything for our vendor review. procurement and security both on the call.
00:00:25 Jamal Reyes (Procurement): hey, thanks. timeline: we need decision by end of feb, ideally.
00:00:35 Diego Rivera (SE): great, thanks. quick agenda: soc2 artifacts, KMS options (CMEK/customer-managed vs redwood-managed), private/VPC deployment for data residency, and then walk through the SIG/CAIQ high-risk items you sent earlier.
00:00:50 Mark Denver (Platform): quick note — we run in eu-west for payments test data, so residency important. also our ops team wants RBAC via SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
00:01:05 Priya Shah (AE): perfect, we'll cover SSO/SCIM too. Lina will handle onboarding, and Diego will dive tech.

00:02:30 Diego Rivera (SE): starting with KMS: Redwood supports two modes: host-managed keys (we handle KMS) and customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS (CMEK). for on-prem or air-gapped, we can integrate HSMs with Private deployment — there are a couple details.
00:02:50 Carolyn Wu (Customer): when you say integrate HSMs, do you mean we can keep keys entirely in our HSM and you never see plaintext? that's, that's the main ask.
00:03:05 Diego Rivera (SE): yes, in Private mode with customer-managed KMS and a suitable KMS proxy we can ensure cryptographic operations are performed in your KMS/HSM and plaintext never leaves your environment. in hosted mode we offer envelope encryption with our-managed keys or bring-your-own-key in cloud KMS. small note: some downstream metadata may still be logged, we have to map those fields for your registry.
00:03:28 Ana Lopez (Compliance): important: audit logs need to be retained for 7 years for some of our merchant datasets. what retention options do you offer?
00:03:40 Diego Rivera (SE): we can configure log retention in Redwood Console, and for private deployments logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. retention windows are configurable; long-term archival may require an extra retention addon or forwarding to S3/Blob you control.
00:03:55 Carolyn Wu (Customer): okay good. and is that covered under SOC 2? can you provide the syslog and audit trail evidence?
00:04:10 Priya Shah (AE): yes we can share SOC 2 Type II and samples of audit logging configuration. we'll redact customer-specific details.

00:07:18 Diego Rivera (SE): switching to SIG/CAIQ mapping — we reviewed your spreadsheet. there were about 12 high-risk items you flagged: encryption at rest, key management, data segregation for multi-tenant, incident response SLA, and access controls. we'll go one by one.
00:07:40 Mark Denver (Customer): for multi-tenant segregation — we need assurance that caches (kv-cache) won't leak across tenants, especially at high throughput. we run bursts.
00:07:55 Diego Rivera (SE): good point — runtime uses tenant-specific namespaces for KV and automatic namespace isolation. in dedicated and private modes we provision separate GPU pools which further isolates compute. there are some corner cases in older model runners where leftovers in GPU memory were possible, but we run a scrub between sessions; we can include that evidence. (slight hesitation) uh — older runner names: legacy-runner 2, i think it's been patched.
00:09:10 Carolyn Wu (Customer): okay, we'd like a short report on that scrub behavior and proof.

00:12:05 Priya Shah (AE): procurement question: pricing and contract: Jamal?
00:12:12 Jamal Reyes (Procurement): yes, question — if we go with private deployment, what's the lead time and cost delta? also, do you have a compliance add-on?
00:12:26 Priya Shah (AE): Private lead time typically 6-8 weeks for standard VPC packages, can be longer for on-prem. Dedicated is faster. there's a compliance package for evidence retention and longer SLA options; Diego will send a breakdown.
00:12:41 Jamal Reyes (Customer): ok that helps.

00:15:00 Diego Rivera (SE): on SSO/SCIM: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC integrates with SAML attributes. for sensitive roles we support step-up MFA via your identity provider. there are nuances with session lifetime for streaming responses — session token TTL is configurable.
00:15:30 Mark Denver (Customer): will SCIM sync user groups to roles automatically or do we map them manually?
00:15:45 Diego Rivera (SE): typically we map SCIM groups to Redwood roles in the console; we can provide a recommended mapping for your org. we also support JIT provisioning if you prefer.

00:20:00 Ana Lopez (Compliance): for the SIG evidence, can you provide a sample of the control implementation doc for 'keys and key lifecycle'? we'd like to see the rotation policy and proof of rotation.
00:20:15 Diego Rivera (SE): yes rotation and KMS lifecycle docs are part of the CMK runbook. rotation is supported; by default cloud KMS rotates yearly, but we can rotate more frequently. we'll provide an example rotation log (anonymized).

00:25:40 Priya Shah (AE): quick check — any competitors you're evaluating that would affect decision?
00:25:50 Carolyn Wu (Customer): we're talking to BigCloud AI and VendorX; BigCloud has a strong native KMS story but higher unit cost.

00:29:05 Diego Rivera (SE): architecture note: for data residency we can pin workloads to eu-west; in Private mode the control plane can run in our region or your region depending on agreement. there are tradeoffs: full control plane locality can add ops overhead.
00:29:30 Mark Denver (Customer): can we do a hybrid where control plane in us-east but data plane pinned to eu-west?
00:29:42 Diego Rivera (SE): hybrid is possible, but then metadata may cross control plane boundaries; we can outline exactly which metadata fields might be replicated and options to minimize that.

00:33:10 Priya Shah (AE): moving to evidence delivery — we'll put artifacts in a secure share. expected artifacts: SOC 2 Type II, architecture diagram, KMS runbook, sample rotation logs, scrub report, RBAC/SCIM config guide, and a short incident response SLA excerpt. does that align with your list?
00:33:28 Carolyn Wu (Customer): yes that's exactly what we need. also a list of subprocessor roster, and a contact for audit requests.
00:33:40 Priya Shah (AE): will include. contact will be Lina Park.

00:37:00 Diego Rivera (SE): small gotcha: for some older community models we have ephemeral caches that can't be encrypted at-rest without performance impact. for production payment workloads we recommend pinned model families that support KV encryption. i'll mark those in the evidence doc.
00:37:20 Carolyn Wu (Customer): good to know. we won't use experimental models.

00:40:55 Ana Lopez (Compliance): on legal — can you accept a vendor addendum for data processing? and do you sign it or do you require redlines?
00:41:05 Priya Shah (AE): we have a standard DPA and can review customer addenda; we'll flag any clauses that require legal escalation. procurement — Jamal can coordinate.
00:41:20 Jamal Reyes (Procurement): will do.

00:45:30 Diego Rivera (SE): question from our side — could you share a sanitized flow of your payment data that touches the model? understanding what fields are sent will help us map controls.
00:45:45 Mark Denver (Customer): yeah i'll get a redacted sample and data flow diagram.

00:49:00 Priya Shah (AE): recap: we'll deliver SOC 2 by 2026-01-20, KMS runbook and TF examples by 2026-01-22, schedule pilot the week of 2026-01-26, provide scrub report and architecture diagram. Oakfield will return SIG spreadsheet updated by 2026-01-18. procurement timeline end-feb.
00:49:20 Carolyn Wu (Customer): that works. one more Q: do you offer SLA credits for downtime that affects payments?
00:49:30 Priya Shah (AE): yes enterprise SLAs and credits are available in Dedicated/Private plans; we'll include the SLA matrix.

00:53:10 Lina Park (CSM): i'll share the onboarding checklist and support contacts after the call.
00:53:25 Diego Rivera (SE): i'll also include a short test plan for KMS validation so you can run the pilot without needing a full deploy.
00:53:40 Priya Shah (AE): great — anyone else?
00:53:50 Jamal Reyes (Procurement): no, thanks, good session.
00:54:05 Carolyn Wu (Customer): thanks everyone.
00:57:10 Notes Bot (recorder): call ended at 16:58 PST
